title: Simultaneous regular parameters for a boundary-compatible regular flag
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], and let $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ be distinct members of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], allowing $r=0$. Let $P\subseteq Q\subsetneq R$ be ideals such that $R/P$ and $R/Q$ are regular local. Assume separately for each $L\in\{P,Q\}$ that there is a regular system of parameters of $R$ containing all the $b_i$ up to multiplication by units and generating $L$ by a subset of its members. Then there is one regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ containing all the $b_i$ up to multiplication by units, and integers $0\le m\le l\le d$, such that $P=(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$ and $Q=(t_1,\ldots,t_l)$. Equality $P=Q$, the zero ideal, empty boundary, and dimension zero are allowed.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121: the simultaneous choice of parameters for V inside Y and the boundary at the start of its proof; the regular-quotient parameter argument is written in Stacks algebra.tex, lemma-regular-quotient-regular.

proof.text: Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$, $V=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and $d=\dim R$. The cotangent-dimension lemma gives $\dim_k V=d$. Rescale the members of each separately adapted parameter system by units so that the specified members are exactly the $b_i$; rescaling does not change any generated ideal. For $L=P,Q$ choose such a system $z^L_1,\ldots,z^L_d$, with $L$ generated by the members indexed by $A_L$. Their classes span $V$, since they generate $\mathfrak m$, and are a basis since there are $d$ of them. In particular the family $E=\{\bar b_i\}$ is independent. Put $U_L=(L+\mathfrak m^2)/\mathfrak m^2\subseteq V$ and $E_L=\{\bar b_i:b_i\in L\}$. Expanding in the adapted basis shows that $U_L$ is the coordinate span of the $z^L_j$ for $j\in A_L$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, first sentence of proof; cotangent method of VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120. Details supplied by Q14.

proof.text: For each $L$, the natural map $L/\mathfrak mL\to V$ is injective with image $U_L$. Indeed write $x\in L\cap\mathfrak m^2$ as $x=\sum_{j\in A_L}a_jz^L_j$. Independence of their classes forces every $a_j\in\mathfrak m$, so $x\in\mathfrak mL$; the reverse inclusion in the kernel and surjectivity onto $U_L$ follow directly from the definitions. In the same adapted basis a member $b_i$ has class in $U_L$ exactly when its coordinate index belongs to $A_L$, exactly when $b_i\in L$. Consequently $\operatorname{span}_k(E)\cap U_L=\operatorname{span}_k(E_L)$. These equalities use the actual separately adapted systems; regularity of the quotients alone would not justify compatibility with the fixed boundary. Also $U_P\subseteq U_Q$ and $E_P\subseteq E_Q$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, first sentence of proof; cotangent method of VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120. Details supplied by Q14.

proof.text: Extend $E_P$ to a basis $A$ of $U_P$ using the basis-extension lemma. The union $A\cup(E_Q\setminus E_P)$ is independent in $U_Q$: in a relation, the sum of the terms from $E_Q\setminus E_P$ lies in $\operatorname{span}(E)\cap U_P=\operatorname{span}(E_P)$, so independence of $E$ makes those coefficients zero, after which independence of $A$ makes the rest zero. Extend this union to a basis $C$ of $U_Q$. The union $C\cup(E\setminus E_Q)$ is independent in $V$ by precisely the same relation argument, now using $\operatorname{span}(E)\cap U_Q=\operatorname{span}(E_Q)$: the coefficients outside $E_Q$ vanish first, and then those in $C$ vanish. Extend it to a basis $T$ of $V$. Thus $A\subseteq C\subseteq T$ and $E\subseteq T$; every extension is an application of the cited statement in the indicated vector space.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, first sentence of proof; cotangent method of VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120. Details supplied by Q14.

proof.text: Choose representatives of $A$ in $P$, of $C\setminus A$ in $Q$, and of $T\setminus C$ in $\mathfrak m$, using the definitions of $U_P,U_Q,V$. Whenever a vector is $\bar b_i$, choose the representative to be exactly $b_i$. This respects those three choices: Step 2 places $\bar b_i$ in $U_P$ or $U_Q$ exactly when $b_i$ belongs to that ideal. By Step 2 the representatives of $A$ give a basis of $P/\mathfrak mP$, and those of $C$ a basis of $Q/\mathfrak mQ$. Apply Nakayama to the finite $R$-modules $P$ and $Q$ to conclude that these representatives generate their respective ideals. Their finiteness follows already from the chosen finite generating subfamilies $z^L_j$. Apply Nakayama to the finite module $\mathfrak m$ as well: the representatives of $T$, whose classes are a basis of $V$, generate $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, first sentence of proof; cotangent method of VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120. Details supplied by Q14.

proof.text: The finite basis $T$ has $d$ members. Enumerate its chosen representatives with those of $A$ first, then $C\setminus A$, then $T\setminus C$. Set $m=|A|$ and $l=|C|$. Step 4 gives $P=(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$ and $Q=(t_1,\ldots,t_l)$; $0\le m\le l\le d$. The full list generates $\mathfrak m$ and has length $d$, hence is a regular system of parameters by definition, containing all $b_i$ exactly. Empty sets and equal subspaces require no extension vectors, so the construction includes $P=Q$, $P=0$, $r=0$, and $d=0$ (where both ideals and the parameter list are zero/empty).

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, first sentence of proof; cotangent method of VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120. Details supplied by Q14.

lean.statement: theorem exists_boundary_regular_flag_parameters {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] (b : List R) (hb : b.Nodup) (hbparams : ∃ s : List R, IsRegularSystemOfParameters s ∧ b ⊆ s) (P Q : Ideal R) (hPQ : P ≤ Q) (hQ : Q ≠ ⊤) (hPregular : IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ P)) (hQregular : IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ Q)) (hadapted : ∀ L : Ideal R, L = P ∨ L = Q → ∃ s : List R, IsRegularSystemOfParameters s ∧ (∀ x ∈ b, ∃ y ∈ s, ∃ a : Rˣ, x = (a : R) * y) ∧ ∃ S : Set R, S ⊆ {x | x ∈ s} ∧ L = Ideal.span S) : ∃ t : List R, IsRegularSystemOfParameters t ∧ (∀ x ∈ b, ∃ y ∈ t, ∃ a : Rˣ, x = (a : R) * y) ∧ ∃ m l : ℕ, m ≤ l ∧ l ≤ t.length ∧ P = Ideal.span {x | x ∈ t.take m} ∧ Q = Ideal.span {x | x ∈ t.take l}

reviewed_lean.note: Lean statement matches the node clause by clause: IsRegularLocalRing R (universe u); Nodup boundary list inside a regular system of parameters; P ≤ Q, Q ≠ ⊤; both quotients regular local; separately adapted systems (units, generating subset); one t with cut points m ≤ l ≤ t.length whose prefixes generate P and Q. Two boundary elements cannot share one parameter up to units, since their cotangent classes are independent. Edge cases P=Q, P=0, empty boundary and d=0 are covered.
